scenario: Admitted 3 nights for pneumonia; policy 2 years old.
cited_clauses: Section 2.1; Section 3.1; Section 3.2; Section 3.3; Section 5.1-5.7; Section 4.1, Section 4.2
summary: The three‑night pneumonia hospitalisation is covered under the in‑patient hospitalisation clause, the initial waiting period is satisfied and no exclusion applies.

scenario: Hospitalised for dengue; policy started 15 days ago.
summary: The claim is denied because the 30‑day initial waiting period for illnesses has not been met (policy is only 15 days old).

scenario: Broke a leg in a road accident; policy is 10 days old.
summary: The broken leg from a road accident is covered because inpatient hospitalisation for injury is included and the initial waiting period does not apply to accidents.

scenario: Diabetic for 5 years; admitted for a diabetes complication; policy 12 months old.
cited_clauses: Section 2.1; Section 3.1; Section 1.2; Section 3.3; Section 5; Section 4.2
summary: The diabetes complication hospitalisation is covered because it meets the in‑patient hospitalisation clause and all waiting periods and exclusions are satisfied.

scenario: Cataract surgery; policy 18 months old.
summary: Cataract surgery is excluded because the policy has a 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period and the policy is only 18 months old.

scenario: Cataract surgery; policy 3 years old.
summary: Cataract surgery is covered because the policy’s hospitalisation benefit applies and the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period is satisfied, though the claim is subject to a Rs 40,000 per‑eye sub‑limit.

scenario: Father, 65, admitted for cardiac care; policy 4 years old.
cited_clauses: Section 2.1; Section 3.1; Section 3.2; Section 3.3; Section 2.3-2.4; Section 5; Section 4.2
summary: The cardiac hospitalisation is covered, but a 10% co‑payment and room‑rent caps will apply.

scenario: Chose a deluxe room costing above 1% of the sum insured.
summary: Deluxe room charges above the 1% daily cap are covered, but the insurer will pay only up to the capped amount proportionately.

scenario: Elective cosmetic nose reshaping.
summary: Elective cosmetic nose reshaping is excluded under the policy’s cosmetic surgery exclusion.

scenario: Reconstructive surgery after a burn injury.
summary: Reconstructive surgery after a burn is covered as an in‑patient hospitalisation expense, with the cosmetic‑surgery exclusion not applying because the surgery is necessitated by the burn.

scenario: Root canal at the dentist; no accident involved.
summary: Root canal (dental) treatment is excluded because dental procedures are not covered unless caused by an accident and requiring hospitalisation.

scenario: Jaw surgery with hospitalisation after a road accident.
summary: Jaw surgery after a road accident is covered under the in‑patient hospitalisation benefit.

scenario: Admitted one day only for tests; no active treatment given.
summary: The admission was only for diagnostic tests with no active treatment, which is expressly excluded under the policy.

scenario: Cataract done as a day-care procedure (<24 hrs); policy 3 years old.
summary: Cataract day‑care surgery is covered, the policy age exceeds the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period, and no exclusion applies, though a Rs 40,000 per‑eye sub‑limit applies.

scenario: Normal delivery; policy 30 months old.
summary: Normal delivery is covered after the 24‑month maternity waiting period, subject to the Rs 50,000 maternity limit.

scenario: Delivery; policy 12 months old.
summary: Maternity expenses are not payable because the policy has only been in force for 12 months, which is less than the required 24‑month maternity waiting period.

scenario: Ambulance bill of Rs 3,500.
summary: Ambulance charges are covered but only up to the Rs 2,000 sub‑limit, so the Rs 3,500 claim will be partially payable.

scenario: Inpatient Ayurvedic treatment at a recognised hospital.
summary: Ayurvedic inpatient treatment is covered, but the claim may be blocked by the 30‑day initial waiting period because the policy age is not provided.

scenario: Rehab for alcohol dependence.
summary: Treatment for alcoholism is expressly excluded, so the rehab claim will not be payable.

scenario: Injury from a suicide attempt.
summary: The policy explicitly excludes expenses from self‑inflicted injury or suicide, so the claim is not payable.

scenario: Cost of new prescription glasses.
summary: Prescription glasses are excluded under the policy’s exclusions.

scenario: Diagnostic tests 20 days before admission.
summary: Pre‑hospitalisation diagnostic tests 20 days before admission are covered, but it’s unclear whether the required initial waiting period has been satisfied because the policy age isn’t provided.

scenario: Medicines bought 75 days after discharge.
summary: Medicines purchased 75 days after discharge are outside the 60‑day post‑hospitalisation coverage window.
